source.title: SynthSAEBench: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders on Scalable Realistic Synthetic Data

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates SAE recovery against known synthetic ground-truth features, bearing on whether SAE features recover the represented units. It does not train a toy network to discover or store features, and it constructs rather than tests the superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The study builds superposition into a synthetic feature dictionary and evaluates trained SAEs on it. Those results test feature recovery in this setting, but do not test whether networks themselves adopt the claimed geometry or the claimed sparsity- and importance-dependent allocation. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: No neural network is studied. SAEs are trained on synthetic activations with known linear ground-truth features under imposed superposition. Their latents are scored against the true features (probing F1, MCC). Even in this best case, recovery is clearly incomplete, which bears on whether dictionary features are complete, canonical units (V5). V1–V4 and V6 are built into the generator, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also argue that, because the LRH holds by construction yet recovery is still imperfect, the bottleneck lies in SAE architectures and training rather than in the representation hypothesis. They attribute part of the failure to feature hedging caused by the SAE being narrower than the true feature count.
record.recipe_differences: The study generates a fixed synthetic feature dictionary with controlled overlap and trains/evaluates SAEs; it does not reproduce the original toy-network optimization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE architecture, SAE L0, hidden dimension/superposition level, feature correlation, firing probabilities and magnitudes, and hierarchy settings affect reported SAE outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: MP-SAEs raise variance explained while F1 and MCC fall as superposition grows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More expressive SAE encoders can fit superposition noise and improve reconstruction without learning the true features.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, Seoul, South Korea, 2026
record.problems: The experiments use a simplified synthetic generator rather than real model representations; the feature geometry and linear-feature assumption are imposed by construction. SAE outcome values are mainly plotted rather than tabulated, and the reported main comparisons use 5 seeds.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-version results were identified. Other SAE metrics and ablations concern SAE benchmark performance but do not directly test the versions beyond the feature-recovery results recorded here.

untested.parts: Seed-to-seed stability of learned features (only seed stdev of metrics is reported); canonicality across widths; any real-model representation.
Whether trained networks adopt superposed geometry or a sparsity-dependent transition. Superposition is imposed by random near-orthogonal directions; Appendix K is analytic only.
Capacity or importance-based allocation in networks.
No LLM activations are analysed; the SAEBench Gemma metrics in Appendix J are cited, not new results.
Features are 1-D by construction; manifold or multi-dimensional features are left to future work.

missing.what: F1 and MCC for BatchTopK, JumpReLU, L1 and MP SAEs on the base benchmark, all below Matryoshka.
Supervised logistic probe F1 0.974 and AUC 0.9999 as the comparison for SAE probing.
F1 and MCC versus superposition level for the non-MP architectures.
Stronger feature correlation slightly lowers F1 (SAEs mix correlated features); high firing-magnitude stdev raises MCC but lowers F1 for all SAEs.
Feature uniqueness of SAE latents, i.e. the fraction tracking distinct true features.

record.verdict_notes: I changed the tranche from T2 to T5: the results show that V5 is partial rather than replicating a method. This verdict rests on synthetic data only; no trained model's representations are examined. Most values are figure-read trends rather than tabulated numbers.

versions.untested_parts: Whether trained toy networks store excess sparse features as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions; sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry. Superposition is imposed in the generated dictionary.

Whether neurons become polysemantic because of capacity pressure, and whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions. The study evaluates SAE architectures, not neuron allocation by importance.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
No LLM representation is directly analyzed for feature spreading across neurons or SAE-recoverable sparse features.
The study measures SAE recovery against known synthetic features, but does not test feature stability or whether SAE features are canonical units in real models.
Features are one-dimensional directions by construction; the study does not compare them with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Matryoshka BatchTopK SAE
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated SAE latent feature classification against ground-truth feature firings.

conditions.value: varied from 15 to 45; 5 seeds per L0

rows.measure: Mean probing F1 score for ground-truth feature firings
rows.value: Peaks at around 0.88; best-performing architecture, while no SAE achieves near-perfect probing F1.
rows.uncertainty: Shaded area is stdev with 5 seeds; numerical stdev not stated.
rows.note: The authors describe imperfect recovery across the tested L0 range; the exact plotted values are not tabulated.
rows.check: The baseline should be the supervised logistic-regression probe on the same activations: mean F1 0.974 (Table 1), against the best SAE F1 of about 0.88. The row covers only the best architecture; the others score lower (Fig. 5).

rows.subject: Matching Pursuit (MP) SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated decoder feature recovery as superposition level changed.
rows.measure: Probing F1 score against ground-truth feature firings
rows.value: Figure only; the text states that F1 decreases as superposition noise increases.
rows.uncertainty: Figure shows shaded standard deviation; numerical values not stated.
rows.note: This indicates weaker ground-truth feature recovery as superposition increases, not a direct measurement of network storage geometry.
rows.check: Figure-only trend in Fig. 7: F1 falls as ρmm rises from about 0.10 to 0.25. The other architectures in the same figure are not recorded.

rows.subject: Matching Pursuit (MP) SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated decoder feature recovery as superposition level changed.
rows.measure: Mean Correlation Coefficient (MCC) against ground-truth feature directions
rows.value: Figure only; the text states that MCC decreases as superposition noise increases.
rows.uncertainty: Figure shows shaded standard deviation; numerical values not stated.
rows.note: The study measures recovery quality separately from reconstruction quality.
rows.check: Figure-only trend in Fig. 7: MCC falls as superposition rises. It reads as worsening alignment of decoder directions with the true features.

rows.subject: Matching Pursuit (MP) SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Measured reconstruction as superposition level changed.
rows.value: Figure only; the text states that variance explained increases as superposition noise increases.
rows.uncertainty: Figure shows shaded standard deviation; numerical values not stated.
rows.note: The authors interpret this alongside declining MCC and F1 as MP-SAEs exploiting superposition noise to improve reconstruction without learning ground-truth features.
rows.check: Reconstruction only. This is an SAE method property, not a measure of feature recovery.

relationships.condition: SAEs (width 4096, narrower than 16,384 true features) on synthetic LRH-by-construction data
relationships.reason: Best SAE probing F1 is about 0.88, against 0.974 for supervised probes; F1 and MCC fall as superposition increases (r1–r3). SAE latents are therefore incomplete proxies for the true units, even in the ideal case.
relationships.display_finding: The best SAE reached probing F1 of about 0.88 against 0.974 for supervised probes, and F1 and MCC fell as superposition increased.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: SAE feature recovery is incomplete: the best probing F1 is around 0.88, and MP-SAE recovery metrics decline as superposition increases (r1–r3). Stability and canonicality in real models were not tested.
